routes.label: Evaluate at the two cube roots
Reduce powers three steps at a time

question: Let \(Q(z)\) and \(R(z)\) be the unique polynomials such that \[ \begin{aligned} &z^{2021}+1 \\ &\quad = (z^2+z+1)Q(z)+R(z) \end{aligned} \] and the degree of \(R\) is less than \(2.\) What is \(R(z)?\)
solution:
The divisor is a factor of \(z^3-1\), so powers whose exponents differ by three have the same remainder.

Write \(D(z)=z^2+z+1\). For every nonnegative integer \(k\),
\[
z^{k+3}-z^k=z^k(z^3-1)=z^k(z-1)D(z).
\]
Thus replacing \(z^{k+3}\) with \(z^k\) changes the polynomial by a multiple of the divisor and leaves its remainder unchanged.

Since \(2021=3\cdot673+2\), repeatedly lowering the exponent by three shows that \(z^{2021}+1\) has the same remainder as \(z^2+1\). Finally,
\[
z^2+1=(z^2+z+1)-z.
\]
The remaining polynomial \(-z\) has degree less than two, as required. Therefore \(\boxed{R(z)=-z}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Substituting a root of the divisor makes the entire quotient term disappear, giving a value of the remainder directly.

The two distinct roots of \(z^2+z+1\) are
\[
\alpha=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2},\qquad
\beta=\frac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2},
\]
where \(i^2=-1\). For either root \(r\), we have \(r^2=-r-1\), so
\[
r^3=-r^2-r=1.
\]
Consequently, using \(2021=3\cdot673+2\),
\[
r^{2021}+1=(r^3)^{673}r^2+1=r^2+1=-r.
\]
Substitution into the given polynomial identity therefore gives \(R(\alpha)=-\alpha\) and \(R(\beta)=-\beta\).

The polynomial \(R(z)+z\) has degree at most one and vanishes at both \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\). A nonzero polynomial of degree at most one cannot have two distinct roots, so \(R(z)+z\) must be identically zero. Hence \(\boxed{R(z)=-z}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Evaluate at the divisor's roots
